review: Individually reviewed all candidate spellings, with targeted inspection of supplied senses for ambiguous homographs and participles. Accept common contemporary Germany-standard nouns, infinitives, adjectives, adverbs, function words, established loanwords and lexicalized colloquial vocabulary. Ordinary capitalized German nouns are valid. Preserve exact candidate tiles, including umlauts and capital sharp S. Reject ordinary inflections, weak specialist/dated/regional homographs, proper/brand names and offensive or vulgar standalone senses. Retain established adjectives with independent current meanings (e.g. GELASSEN, GEBILDET, ANGESEHEN, VERLIEBT), and familiar lexicalized adverbs. Plural-only vocabulary such as LEUTE, ELTERN and NACHRICHTEN is valid; homographs with common infinitives such as SCHULDEN, SCHMERZEN, REIHEN and TRÄNEN are valid. A neutral common sense remains eligible despite an additional vulgar sense (e.g. SCHWANZ as tail). Frequency was supporting evidence, never sufficient on its own. Exclusions are curation decisions, not claims that the spellings are invalid German. The additional 33 sharp-S candidates were separately reviewed after corrected frequency lookup; 29 accepted and four excluded. Final review covers all 2,336 candidates.
